tasks.short: Advise and assist students in office hours, arrange appointments, and send follow-up links and materials.

steps.what: Biology lecturer advises and assists students in office hours
Biology lecturer arranges office-hour appointments by e-mail
Biology lecturer sends follow-up links and materials to students

tasks.design: Students book office-hour slots themselves on the lecturer's booking page ({CALENDAR}), so appointments are not arranged by e-mail. Common follow-up material (practical guides, reading lists, past questions) sits on a course resource page that the lecturer links to. Advising students stays with the lecturer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Appointments were arranged by e-mail back and forth.
tasks.enabler_now: Calendars offer booking pages with set slots.
tasks.still_hard: Students in difficulty do not book slots.
tasks.human_edge: Encouraging a student who is about to drop biology.

evidence.claim: Calendars offer booking pages with set slots.

assumptions: Boundary: from the student visit to the follow-up sent; formal study advice is outside.
Input contract: booking page published; fallback is e-mail.
Students book in less time than e-mailing; a little student time is priced.

incremental.description: Biology lecturer keeps the resource page current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few visits; high: busy weeks before exams.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Search and screen the literature, run experiments, record lab data, analyse data and write the manuscript, format references, check the manuscript, and submit it.

steps.what: Biology lecturer searches and screens literature in the field of knowledge

loop.input: The research question and the library's citation databases.
loop.check: Each title must resolve by DOI or catalogue, else it is dropped; the lecturer chooses what to read.
loop.stop: One search per question; if nothing resolves, the lecturer searches by hand.
loop.why_not_simpler: Topics are described in many ways; keyword search misses related work.

steps.what: Biology lecturer conducts research experiments in the lab
Biology lecturer records lab data in a paper notebook and spreadsheets
Biology lecturer analyses data and writes findings for professional journals
Biology lecturer formats references to the journal's style by hand
Biology lecturer checks the final manuscript
Biology lecturer submits the manuscript to publish findings through the journal portal

tasks.design: A research search tool over the library's citation databases ({OTHER}) suggests related titles; any title that does not resolve by DOI or catalogue is dropped. Lab data go into an electronic lab notebook ({DATA_PLATFORM}) with instrument files imported, so data are not copied from paper into spreadsheets. A reference manager formats citations in the journal's style. Experiments, analysis, writing and submitting stay with the lecturer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Literature was searched by keyword, lab data copied from paper and references formatted by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Citation databases suggest related work; electronic lab notebooks import instrument files.
tasks.still_hard: Field observations still start on paper.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing which odd result is worth a new experiment.
tasks.altitude: The lecturer spends more time on experiments and writing.

evidence.claim: Scopus AI gives topic summaries and foundational papers.
Electronic lab notebooks can import instrument files.
Funder rules bar referees from using generative AI on proposals.

assumptions: Boundary: from the research question to the manuscript submitted; peer review is outside.
Input contract: notebook licensed by the university; fallback is paper.
The lecturer writes and submits every manuscript.
research_questions: Do suggested titles add work the lecturer would have missed?

incremental.description: Biology lecturer sets up notebook templates per experiment type.

approvals.approved_version: The manuscript as checked by the lecturer in s6.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: field work; high: lab work with many instrument files.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Meet colleagues on teaching and research issues, plan the meetings, write and share meeting notes, and co-write shared documents.

steps.what: Biology lecturer collaborates with colleagues in meetings on teaching and research issues
Biology lecturer plans meetings with colleagues by e-mail
Biology lecturer writes and shares meeting notes

loop.input: The recorded meeting, when every participant consents.
loop.output: Draft notes with decisions and actions.
loop.check: Every action must name an owner who was in the meeting; the lecturer edits the notes before sharing.
loop.stop: One draft per meeting; if anyone declines recording, the lecturer writes the notes.
loop.why_not_simpler: Discussions are free-form; a form does not capture them.

steps.what: Biology lecturer co-writes documents by e-mailing versions to colleagues

tasks.design: Meetings are planned with a shared-calendar poll ({CALENDAR}) instead of e-mail rounds. When all participants consent, a transcription tool drafts notes with decisions and actions, and the lecturer edits them before sharing. Shared documents are written together in one online file ({DOCS}) instead of e-mailed versions. Discussing issues with colleagues stays with the lecturer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Meetings were planned by e-mail, notes typed afterwards and versions mailed around.
tasks.enabler_now: Calendar polls, meeting transcription and shared editing are standard.
tasks.human_edge: Finding common ground between colleagues who disagree.

reach.learn: Whether notes and documents are current.

evidence.claim: Meeting tools can transcribe recordings and draft notes; shared editing replaces mailed versions.
Systems able to monitor staff need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the shared issue to the document written; department decisions are outside.
Input contract: consent for recording; fallback is own notes.
Works council consent comes before recording.
research_questions: How much of the drafted notes is changed?

incremental.description: Biology lecturer asks consent for recording.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few recorded meetings; high: frequent project meetings.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compare textbooks and lab equipment, check lab stock, fill the purchase request, check it, send it to purchasing, record the chosen textbook, and receive deliveries.

steps.what: Biology lecturer selects textbooks and laboratory equipment by comparing options
Biology lecturer checks lab stock of supplies by hand
Biology lecturer fills the purchase request to obtain materials and supplies
Biology lecturer checks the final purchase request
Biology lecturer e-mails the request to the purchasing department
Biology lecturer records the chosen textbook in the course reading list
Biology lecturer receives and checks delivered equipment

tasks.design: Lab supplies are tracked in the lab inventory ({DATA_PLATFORM}) with barcodes, so stock is checked on screen. Items are picked from suppliers' punch-out catalogues in the purchasing system ({PROCUREMENT}), which builds the request; once checked, it goes to purchasing in the system. The textbook is added to the course reading list tool from the library catalogue instead of typed. Choosing materials and checking deliveries stay with the lecturer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Stock was checked by hand, requests typed and mailed, and reading lists typed.
tasks.enabler_now: Lab inventories, punch-out catalogues and reading list tools are standard.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing the textbook that students will actually read.
tasks.altitude: The lecturer chooses instead of typing requests.

evidence.claim: Lab inventories with barcodes, punch-out catalogues and reading list tools are standard.

assumptions: Boundary: from the course need to the delivery checked; supplier contracts are outside.
Input contract: catalogues connected by purchasing; fallback is typed requests.
Purchasing handles system requests as it did e-mails.
research_questions: Do practicals start with all supplies more often?

incremental.description: Biology lecturer scans supplies into the lab inventory.

approvals.approved_version: The request as checked by the lecturer in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: much special equipment; high: mostly catalogue items.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The biology lecturer keeps advising, doing research, working with colleagues and choosing materials; e-mail scheduling, paper lab data, note typing and typed requests shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A lecturer with more time for research.
